The digital energy stack brings together data, connectivity, compute, digital public infrastructure, AI, and governance to deliver affordable and reliable energy. And at the base of it all sits data.
 
Data shapes how energy investments are planned, how systems are rolled out, and how impact is measured. Yet persistent gaps — from geospatial and consumption data to credit risk, usage, and gender-disaggregated data — continue to slow progress, limit bankability, and reinforce inequality. In many contexts, this is less a technical gap than a structural one. 
 
In this context, we're seeing governments and countries:
 
📊 Strengthen energy baselines, including leveraging innovative data sources to support informed decision-making
🗂️ Undertake data audits to identify data assets and gaps, supported by tools such as UNDP’s Data to Policy Navigator
📈 Refine core energy data collection processes, including improving supply-side knowledge and understanding.
 
👉 Read more about the Digital Energy Stack here: https://lnkd.in/e7PebbrX

We're very interested in hearing about other initiatives, interventions, and insights from countries and #energy stakeholders around the world. How can we support countries in turning data into inclusive energy impact? Let us know in the comments!
